programme: A cholesterol-flux / circadian-output module built from complementary targets: ZNF202 represses the reverse-cholesterol-transport genes ABCA1, ABCG1, APOE and APOA1, while NFIA targets NR1H3 (LXRα), the nuclear receptor that normally activates that same ABCA1/ABCG1 axis — an opposing pair on one node. HLF and KLF9 independently converge on CYP7A1, the rate-limiting enzyme of bile-acid/cholesterol catabolism, and KLF9 additionally targets LDLR, STAR and CYP11A1. RORB targets BMAL1 (the core clock gene RORs canonically activate) and NAMPT, a clock-controlled metabolic gene. MLX carries TXNIP, its signature glucose/lipid-sensing partner gene.
role_in_a: Disrupted cholesterol biosynthesis and clearance, and circadian-rhythm dysfunction detectable in peripheral tissue, are both established, replicated features of Huntington's Disease independent of tissue-specific CAG pathology — consistent with this network being built from blood. NFIA separately marks a maturity/identity shift in HD astrocytes (PMID 36590162), though that paper does not itself discuss cholesterol or clock biology.
role_in_b: Renal cell carcinoma is characteristically associated with rewired lipid and cholesterol handling as part of its metabolic reprogramming, and circadian clock genes are recurrently reported as dysregulated across kidney cancers; NFI-family transcription factors have documented expression/prognostic alterations in kidney and other cancers (PMID 32219034). Both associations are better established for clear-cell than papillary histology, so the attribution to papillary RCC specifically is weaker than to kidney cancer broadly.
shared_axis: If both diseases independently perturb cellular cholesterol handling — HD through impaired biosynthesis/efflux, papillary RCC through tumor metabolic reprogramming — they could converge on the same generic buffering machinery (the ZNF202/NFIA–LXR–ABCA1/ABCG1 node and the clock-linked HLF/KLF9–CYP7A1 and RORB–BMAL1 arms) without sharing an upstream cause.
reasoning: The module is nameable from specific, non-generic shared or complementary targets (CYP7A1 shared by HLF and KLF9; NR1H3/LXR vs. ABCA1/ABCG1 as opposing nodes for NFIA and ZNF202; BMAL1 as RORB's canonical clock target), so this is not twelve factors thrown together. But only NFIA has any retrieved literature placement in either disease, and even that evidence is tangential to cholesterol or clock biology rather than confirming it — so the cross-disease connection rests on established general biology of HD and renal cancer, not on anything retrieved for this specific pair.
support: PMID 36590162 — places NFIA in Huntington's Disease, in the context of astrocyte maturity/identity in HD iPSC and mouse models (not specifically cholesterol or circadian biology). PMID 32219034 — places NFI-family genes in human cancers including a kidney-cancer context, as a general expression/prognostic survey rather than papillary-RCC- or cholesterol-specific evidence. No retrieved evidence for ZNF202, HLF, KLF9, RORB, or MLX in either disease.
how_to_falsify: In matched blood samples from HD patients vs. controls and in papillary RCC tumor vs. adjacent normal kidney (independent cohorts), test whether ABCA1/ABCG1/NR1H3 track with ZNF202/NFIA activity and whether CYP7A1 tracks with HLF/KLF9 activity, and whether BMAL1/NAMPT track with RORB activity. If none of these show coordinated dysregulation with disease state in either tissue, or if direct binding of ZNF202/NFIA/HLF/KLF9/RORB at these specific loci cannot be confirmed by ChIP/CUT&RUN, the module is not operating as described here.
caveats: Blood (HD) and kidney tumor (KIRP) share no cell type, so any real shared axis must run through tissue-general metabolic/circadian machinery, not shared regulatory context. The 294 patient-group comparisons come from only 2 independent cohort pairs, so recurrence fractions reflect overlapping subgroup splits within few cohorts rather than independent replication. ReMap binding evidence exists only for KLF9 (2/23 targets, unspecified which) among the carrying factors, so direct binding at CYP7A1/LDLR specifically is not confirmed by the ChIP data in hand. The tissue-generic exclusion list already removes RORA, STAT1/STAT2/IRF7/IRF8 as ambient clock/immune activity in blood and kidney, so this account should be read as one sub-module rising above that baseline, not a claim that all circadian signal here is disease-specific. Other concordant factors — HEY2 (Notch-driven cardiac/vascular differentiation), FOSL1 (AP-1/MMP inflammatory-invasion programme), FOXD2, ARID4A, ZIC2, LRRFIP1 — are not explained by this account.
